title: Stars trails over Armazones
caption: Star trails over Cerro Armazones, site of the Extremely Large Telescope, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at the ELT site, Cerro Armazones, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Dotted trails of stars run across the sky above the summit of Cerro Armazones, with an instrument standing on the right. The picture combines multiple exposures taken looking west from the top of this 3046-metre-high mountain, the site chosen for ESO's Extremely Large Telescope.

Because Earth rotates, the night sky appears to turn around the southern celestial pole. When a series of exposures is stacked, each star leaves a line of dots along its path. The gaps between the dots mark the breaks between individual frames.

The shape of the trails depends on where they sit in the sky. Toward the celestial equator, which lies near the left edge of this view, the trails run straighter. The instrument on the right is the Differential Image Motion Monitor, or DIMM. It measures atmospheric seeing, the blurring caused by turbulent air, which is a key test of any site for a giant telescope.

understand.summary: This is a stack of night-time photographs taken in visible light with a camera on Cerro Armazones. The exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points; the dotted trails appear only because many separate exposures were combined.

explore: Measuring the seeing before building is essential: a large mirror cannot deliver sharp images if the air above it constantly shimmers, so instruments like the DIMM help confirm that a mountaintop is worth the investment.
alt: Dotted star trails across the night sky above a mountaintop, with a measuring instrument on the right.
